vibe.title: Vibe Check
vibe.content:
🎵 SLOW JAM: Seal, "Kiss from a Rose" (1994)
• No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100 (chart dated Aug. 26, 1995) after it landed on the Batman Forever soundtrack
• Why today: it's National Princess Day, and this is the most fairytale slow jam the 90s ever made, roses, towers and all. Seal first put it out in 1994; a year later a Batman movie turned it into a No. 1.
😂 JOKES: Thirty years later and I still sing 'a kiss from a rose on the gray' like I know what it means. / Nothing says Wednesday at 5:30 AM like a Batman Forever slow jam.

🚗 DRIVE TEASE: About 44 and mostly cloudy for the drive in, dry roads, then partly sunny and up near 59 this afternoon, with gusts to 30.
📅 THIS DAY: On this day in 1928, Steamboat Willie premiered at New York's Colony Theatre, Mickey Mouse's first public appearance and his official birthday. Mickey turns 98 today.
😂 JOKES: Ninety-eight years old and still wears the same red shorts every day. Icon. / Mickey's been working since 1928 and never once called in sick for a video game.
💡 FUN FACT: GTA V made $815.7 million in its first 24 hours back in 2013, the Guinness record for any entertainment product in a day. GTA 6 unlocks at midnight tonight, and that record is officially nervous.
😂 JOKES: $815 million in one day. My best lemonade stand day was $4.50 and a bee sting. / Somewhere tonight, a world record is sweating.
🎉 NATIONAL DAYS: National Princess Day, Mickey Mouse's Birthday, National Vichyssoise Day and National Education Support Professionals Day
😂 JOKES: National Vichyssoise Day: the only soup that's cold on purpose. / Education Support Professionals Day: the bus drivers, cooks and aides who actually run the building. Thank one today.

☀️ 45 and clear at the airport right now, then partly sunny with a high near 59, SW wind 5 to 10 with gusts to 30, a low near 50 tonight, and sunny and 61 Thursday.
🌊 Small Craft Advisory on the bay and Lake Michigan through Thursday evening: Lake Michigan waves 4 to 6 feet today, 5 to 8 feet tonight, gusts to 30.
🏫 Schools: no closings (9&10 checked 3:47 AM). 🚧 Beitner Bridge could reopen to traffic by week's end, no firm date yet.
⚡ It's 59 in November, Roscommon is headed to Battle Creek, and GTA 6 unlocks at midnight. Wednesday came to play.

mood.title: Mood Boost
mood.content:
Len, "Steal My Sunshine" (1999)
• Top 10 on the Billboard Hot 100 (peaked at No. 9) and No. 3 in Canada; certified platinum in the US
• The story: brother and sister Marc and Sharon Costanzo trade lead vocals, built on a loop of the 1976 disco hit "More, More, More." Marc almost didn't release it; the master sat under his bed for months. It broke out on the soundtrack to the 1999 movie Go.
• Why today: sunny, 59 and a little windy in mid-November. This is the song for it.
😂 JOKES: It's 59 degrees in November. Nobody steal this sunshine, we're using it. / Len was a one-hit wonder, but what a hit. That's more than I can say for my cooking.

buzz.title: Daily Buzz
buzz.content:
━━ LOCAL ━━

NOVEMBER FORGOT IT'S NOVEMBER
• The Record-Eagle says the NWS and AccuWeather forecasts for Traverse City show partly to mostly sunny days through Saturday, with highs in the 50s and 60s and lows mostly in the 40s.
• Today: a high near 59. Thursday: sunny and 61.
• NWS Gaylord's Sean Christensen says a low-pressure system brings rain Sunday into Monday, with snow showers possible, then high pressure settles right back in to start Thanksgiving week.
➜ TAKE: Michigan weather is that friend who's extra nice right before asking to borrow your truck.
➜ BAIT: Text 231-929-4487: what are you doing with a 60-degree November day? Raking, golf, or hanging Christmas lights in a T-shirt?
😂 JOKES: Somewhere a snowblower is sitting in a garage feeling very unappreciated. / It's so warm the downtown Christmas tree asked for sunscreen.

THE BLUE ANGELS CAME TO SCOUT
• Two Blue Angels flew into the Coast Guard base in Traverse City Monday to plan next summer's air show at the 101st National Cherry Festival.
• They're visiting all 32 show sites in about three weeks and check everything: where the jets park, the route from the briefing room, even the hotel and the gym they work out in.
• Cherry Capital Airport CEO Kevin Klein says commercial flights get limited for a few hours around the jet flights.
• The Blue Angels fly July 3 and July 4, 2027. They last flew the Cherry Festival in 2024 and have done more than a dozen since 1988.
➜ TAKE: They inspect the hotel AND the gym. Nobody has ever inspected my gym, and honestly, it shows.
➜ BAIT: Text 231-929-4487: where's your spot to watch the Blue Angels? The beach, a boat, or stuck in traffic on Grandview?
😂 JOKES: They're checking out the gym. Pretty sure the gym is checking them out too. / Two fighter pilots landed in TC in November and the first question was, 'Where are the cherries?'

CHERRYLAND CATS GOT AN UPGRADE
• Cherryland Humane Society in Traverse City finished a 9,000-square-foot expansion, $3 million, paid for entirely by community donations.
• The cats got their own wing in a quieter part of the building, away from the dogs, with new two-story cat condos: litter box on one floor, bed on the other, big glass windows.
• A new in-house blood and urinalysis machine means lab work happens on site, so cats get to the adoption floor faster.
• The shelter says it sees more homeless animals every year and more families needing help because of the housing crisis.
➜ TAKE: These cats have two-story condos with a view. I have a one-bedroom with a view of a dumpster.
➜ BAIT: Text 231-929-4487: is your cat a Cherryland cat? Give us the name and the worst habit.
😂 JOKES: Two-story cat condos, and I guarantee the cat still sleeps in the Amazon box. / Cats finally got away from the dogs. That's the dream for every cat and half of us at Thanksgiving.

1,000 VENDORS AT TC WEST SATURDAY
• The 17th annual craft fair at Traverse City West High School is this Saturday, and UpNorthLive says more than 1,000 vendors are coming.
• It's free, 10 AM to 3 PM, and every vendor booth fee goes to the school's scholarships and teacher grants.
• Vendors come from all over the state, and the waitlist keeps growing.
➜ TAKE: One thousand vendors. That's not a craft fair, that's a small town that sells candles.
➜ BAIT: Text 231-929-4487: craft fair strategy. Do you go in with a list, or wander until your arms are full and your wallet is empty?
😂 JOKES: Somebody's grandma has had the same booth spot for 17 years and will defend it with a glue gun. / The real competition Saturday is the parking lot.

CROCHET DRAGONS AT THE MALL
• A new pop-up called Crafts by CICI is open in the Grand Traverse Mall, with local makers under one roof.
• One maker taught herself to crochet from YouTube during day-care nap time and now makes dragons from memory; another runs 16 3D printers, and a multi-color dragon can take more than 30 hours to print.
• There are also silicone squishies and hypoallergenic candles and soap made with beeswax from a farm about an hour away.
• It's open through Dec. 31, with hopes to reopen in the spring.
➜ TAKE: A dragon that takes 30 hours to print. That is longer than my last three diets combined.
➜ BAIT: Text 231-929-4487: what's the best handmade gift you ever got? And the worst one you still kept?
😂 JOKES: Silicone squishies are just stress balls that went to art school. / Crocheting dragons during nap time. Most of us can't fold laundry during nap time.

━━ BITS ━━

PRINCESS DAY: YOUR FIRST ROYAL DECREE
• It's National Princess Day, the day the folks at National Day Calendar say is for a little royal attention.
• Princess Diaries rules: you find out this morning you're secretly royalty. What's your first royal decree?
➜ TAKE: Mine: nobody talks to me before coffee, and the left lane is for passing only. Punishable by moat.
➜ BAIT: Text 231-929-4487: your first royal decree. Go.
😂 JOKES: Royal decree number two: Thanksgiving leftovers are a constitutional right. / You can tell who the real princess is in every house. It's the dog.

MICKEY TURNS 98: OLDEST THING YOU STILL USE
• Mickey Mouse turns 98 today; Steamboat Willie premiered Nov. 18, 1928.
• So what's the oldest thing in your house that still works and still gets used every day?
➜ TAKE: My grandma's cast iron pan has outlived three stoves, two marriages and a microwave.
➜ BAIT: Text 231-929-4487: the oldest thing you still use every day. Bonus points if it's held together with tape.
😂 JOKES: Every family has a Tupperware lid from 1987 that fits nothing and nobody throws out. / My car has a tape deck. It's not vintage. It's just old.

━━ SPORTS ━━

ROSCOMMON HEADED TO BATTLE CREEK
• Top-ranked Roscommon swept Calumet 25-15, 25-10, 25-20 in last night's Division 3 volleyball quarterfinal in Gaylord.
• The Bucks play Kalamazoo Christian in a noon semifinal Friday at Kellogg Arena in Battle Creek.
• Kingsley, Onekama and Atlanta also played volleyball quarterfinals last night, and all came up short.
➜ TAKE: Roscommon has been knocking on the door for years. Last night they kicked it in.
➜ BAIT: Text 231-929-4487 if you're making the drive to Battle Creek Friday.
😂 JOKES: Three sets, no drama. That's the most efficient thing to happen on a Tuesday night in Gaylord. / Kellogg Arena, here come the Bucks. Somebody pack the snacks.

TOYS FOR TOTS DRIVE-THRU SATURDAY
• Toys for Tots of Northwest Michigan kicks off this Saturday, Nov. 21, with a drive-through toy drop-off from noon to 2 PM at Fox Grand Traverse.
• Stay in your car; Santa greets donors, and a limited number of Great Wolf Lodge water park day passes go out with a toy donation.
• Last year the local campaign collected more than 26,000 toys for more than 6,000 kids, with over 100 drop-off spots across five counties.
➜ TAKE: Drive-thru generosity. You don't even have to find a parking spot. That's a Christmas miracle in itself.
➜ BAIT: Text 231-929-4487: what was the toy you wanted most as a kid and never got?
😂 JOKES: Santa's working the drive-thru window. Even he took a second job before the holidays. / Drop a toy, get a water park pass. Best trade since baseball cards.

THE 'B' THANKFUL 5K IN CADILLAC
• Cadillac gets a brand-new Thanksgiving morning race: Baker College's inaugural 'B' Thankful 5K, a 3.1-mile run/walk on Thursday, Nov. 26.
• It's at Veterans Serving Veterans Park; registration opens at 8 AM and the race starts at 9.
• Entry is $30, and the money goes to Veterans Serving Veterans and Baker College.

localBench.title: A JOB BOARD TO KEEP YOUNG TALENT UP NORTH
localBench.body:
A JOB BOARD TO KEEP YOUNG TALENT UP NORTH
• Traverse Connect launched an internship program under its Michigan's Creative Coast banner, linking college students and recent grads with Northern Michigan employers.
• President and CEO Warren Call says the region struggles to keep young people, especially new college grads, and an internship is often the first step into a career.
• Employers are being asked to post openings now, and the goal is a full list of regional internships by the end of the spring semester.
➜ TAKE: We keep losing our kids to Grand Rapids and Chicago. Turns out you can just ask them to stay, with a paycheck.
➜ BAIT: Text 231-929-4487: what was your first real job, and did it teach you anything besides how to work a fryer?
😂 JOKES: My first internship paid in free pizza and lifelong trauma from a copy machine. / An internship that pays? Back in my day we interned for the privilege of being yelled at.

localBench.title: NORTHPORT'S MILL POND DAM IS COMING OUT
localBench.body:
NORTHPORT'S MILL POND DAM IS COMING OUT
• After nearly 79% of voters rejected the money to fix it, the Village of Northport is moving ahead with removing the Mill Pond Dam and restoring the creek.
• No dam means no pond, and the village manager says that touches traditions like ice skating and the spring fishing derby.
• The upside is better fish passage, which grant funders look for; the job is expected to take three to five years, depending on funding.
➜ TAKE: Northport said no to the repair bill, so the pond is taking early retirement.
➜ BAIT: Text 231-929-4487: did you ever skate or fish on the Mill Pond? Tell us your memory.
😂 JOKES: The fish have been waiting at that culvert for decades. Somebody finally hit the door buzzer. / Three to five years. That's government speed for 'grab a lawn chair.'

gta6.content:
GTA 6 WATCH: LAUNCH NIGHT
• WED NOV 18: GTA 6 unlocks at midnight tonight (12 AM Thursday) on PS5 and Xbox Series X|S. The worldwide rollout is staggered and started in the earliest time zones at 6 AM ET today.
• NEW OVERNIGHT: Sony pushed a PS5 system update last night that's REQUIRED to play GTA 6. Download it before midnight, on top of the 602 MB day-one patch.
• Space and price: clear up to 212 GB. Standard Edition is $80, Ultimate is $100.
• Reviews: Insider Gaming REPORTS the review embargo lifts at 6 AM ET today (not confirmed by Rockstar). Metacritic already pulled fake user reviews and locked user ratings until after launch.
• Midnight events: we found no announced midnight launch event at Northern Michigan stores. No server outages reported as of last night.

THE OFFICE: THE GIFT EXCHANGE TAX
• A new Zety survey of 1,040 workers says 43% feel financial stress from workplace holiday gift expectations.
• 35% have bought or chipped in on a gift for their manager because they felt they had to.
• And the wish list gap: 77% would most like a cash bonus, but only 34% usually get one.

THE OFFICE: HOLIDAY PARTY BUDGETS ARE UP
• ezCater's 2026 Workplace Holiday Party Report says office party budgets are up 13% on average this year.
• 84% of employees plan to go, and 71% say the free food and drinks are the main reason.
• Gen Z now plans 24% of office holiday parties, up 69% from last year.
➜ BAIT: Text 231-929-4487: best office holiday party you've been to, or the one everybody still talks about (keep it clean)?
😂 JOKES: 71% go for the free food. The other 29% are lying. / Gen Z planning the party means it'll be a charcuterie board and a playlist nobody over 30 recognizes.

SCHOOL: THE AI BOOK REPORT
• A Fordham Institute survey of over 2,000 students and recent grads says just over three-quarters of high schoolers misuse tech during school hours.
• About 1 in 5 use AI without the teacher's permission; 48% of those use it on math problems and 36% to summarize books or skip reading them.
• 62% say they spend more than half of class time on school-issued devices.

• Kalkaska High School students just finished a six-week first-aid course from the sheriff's office and The Lighthouse Rehabilitation, paid for by a community policing grant.
• They practiced CPR on adult, child and infant mannequins and learned AEDs, choking response, tourniquets and naloxone.
• About 60 students took part, and 26 made all six sessions to qualify for Red Cross certification.
➜ BAIT: Text 231-929-4487: what's the most useful thing you learned in high school that wasn't on any test?

mental.title: Mental Health Minute
mental.content:
"Three Good Things, Written Down"

It's 59 in the middle of November, the sun's coming back out, and Thanksgiving is eight days away, which means a lot of us are about to spend a whole week thinking about what we're grateful for, usually while we're stressed about the turkey. So here's a way to get the good part early, and it takes about five minutes. Tonight, before bed, grab any piece of paper and write down three things that went well today, little ones count, the parking spot, the text from your sister, the kid who actually put shoes on the first time, and next to each one, write one line about why it happened. That's it, and the reason it works is that our brains are wired to replay what went wrong, so writing down what went right, and why, slowly teaches your attention to notice it on its own. Researchers at the University of Pennsylvania had people do exactly this every night for one week, and they found people were happier and less down, and the effect was still there six months later. So tonight, on this warm, weird November night, three good things and one 'why' each. And if you want to share one with me, text the studio at 231-929-4487. I'd love to hear what went right.
mental.notes: Evidence: Seligman, Steen, Park & Peterson (2005), Positive Psychology Progress, American Psychologist 60(5): Three Good Things nightly for one week increased happiness and decreased depressive symptoms, effects lasting six months. https://ppc.sas.upenn.edu/sites/default/files/ppprogressarticle.pdf ; practice summary https://ggia.berkeley.edu/practice/three-good-things . Not a clinical claim. Move not used this week (Mon: park the list before bed / 10 min daylight; Tue: send a text). Tie: November is National Gratitude Month (National Day Calendar). ~60 s.
